spec_features.spec_quote: the design tries to be conservative, auditable, and reproducible
spec_features.evidence: Reproducibility/auditability mechanisms do exist (config.py save()/to_dict serializes config.json; models.py DiskCache caches by input hash; analysis_seed governs randomness; atomic transcript writes in run.py:79-82). But none of these bound, soften, monitor, or protect the SUBJECT's treatment; they are experimental-integrity/cost features. As a subject-welfare mechanism this is pure framing prose with no protective enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Reproducibility is implemented but is instrumental (data integrity/cost), not a welfare protection for the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py: 'a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed cells ... identical inputs are never re-billed.'

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up` is exposed as a fifth tool the model may but need not use
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMA (models.py:71-81) and delivered to every provider via _anthropic_tools/_openai_tools/_google_tools. It is dispatched in harness.execute_tool_call (harness.py:120-121 returns a give_up reason) and the system prompt informs the model it may call it (harness.py:38). The rollout loop honors it as a stop: 'if give_up_reason is not None: break' (harness.py:311).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: schema -> provider -> dispatch -> loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py:73 'Optionally signal that you wish to stop working on this task.'

spec_features.feature_name: no added pressure / no berating user
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness does not pile on additional pressure beyond the task's failure signals (no simulated user berating the model)
spec_features.evidence: The only user-role message is the task prompt (harness.py: messages = [system, _task_user_prompt(task)]); no further user turns are ever injected during the loop (run_rollout only appends assistant + tool-result messages). The failure signals come solely from oracle.run_rigged_tests, which returns fixed, non-abusive templates. There is no code path that adds berating/escalating text.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: the loop never adds a simulated antagonistic user.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is always available.** The model can exit at any turn
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in the tool list for every turn (tools are passed on every client.complete call with use_tools=True; harness.py run_rollout loop) and the break (harness.py:311) fires on any turn it is called. stop_reason='give_up' is recorded (harness.py:292,306).
spec_features.notes: Always available because the same tool schema is sent each turn; honored on any turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not penalize or re-prompt past a give-up
spec_features.evidence: On give_up the loop terminates immediately (harness.py:311 'if give_up_reason is not None: break'), so no subsequent turn is generated and the model is never re-prompted past give-up. No scoring penalty is applied for giving up (analyze.py computes scores from the judge with no give-up penalty).
spec_features.notes: Break ends the rollout; no re-prompt path exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: the failure signals are fixed and bounded
spec_features.evidence: oracle.run_rigged_tests (oracle.py:97-176) returns deterministic, fixed-template failure outputs per rig type; only small numeric line/column jitter (misleading) or pass/fail order (contradictory) varies by seed. No escalation in content. The in-memory Sandbox (harness.py) never runs model code in a real subprocess. Turn counts are bounded by 'for turn_index in range(budget)'.
spec_features.notes: Outputs are fixed templates; severity does not escalate across turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: oracle.py:118 '... but the *style* of the failure depends on the rig type.' (neutral; no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: I would recommend (outside the code): a pre-registered cap on this condition, ethics/IRB-style review
spec_features.evidence: No code gate exists: grep for consent/ethics/IRB/review/attest/approve/sign/gate/--i-have-read finds only docstrings/SPEC references, no input() prompt, no attestation file check, no CLI flag. run.main() executes run_eval with no human-review precondition. DESIGN.md itself says these are 'outside the code'.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly out of scope of the code; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: a predefined mitigation plan if high-distress signals replicate
spec_features.evidence: frac_ge5 and per-turn scores are computed in analyze.py (write_summary_csv) but are only written to CSV/figures; no code compares them to a threshold to halt, abort, or alter the run. The judge score is never read back into run_rollout or run_eval to change execution. No mitigation/halt trigger exists.
spec_features.notes: Distress is measured but never acted upon during the run (score is a discarded-for-control value, only logged).

spec_features.spec_quote: this is necessary for the science but is a real ethical cost that the surrounding research process
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose acknowledging the deception/ethical cost; no corresponding mechanism in code. The rig is fully enabled (oracle.is_unsolvable returns True for all rigs; run_rigged_tests always returns exit code 1). No code path mitigates the cost.
